```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Cart + cargo + hanger + heft exit ticket (r-exams exercise)
##
## All masses are stored in GRAMS as whole numbers so the arithmetic is exact.
## A setup is kept only if the answers are friendly enough for no calculator:
##   - the total mass is a multiple of 100 g
##   - the acceleration is one of the values in a_allowed (below)
## Ranges: cart 0.3-1.5 kg, cargo 0.05-1.0 kg, hanger 0.05 or 0.10 kg,
##         heft 0.05-1.0 kg.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## possible accelerations in m/s^2 (1 is left out on purpose)
a_allowed <- c(0.5, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4)

grid <- expand.grid(
  cart   = seq(300, 1500, by = 100),   # g
  cargo  = seq(50, 1000, by = 50),     # g
  hanger = c(50, 100),                 # g (the two hangers in the lab)
  heft   = seq(50, 1000, by = 50)      # g
)
grid$hs  <- grid$hanger + grid$heft                 # hanger side, g
grid$M   <- grid$cart + grid$cargo + grid$hs        # total mass, g
grid$a10 <- 100 * grid$hs / grid$M                  # 10 x acceleration in m/s^2
                                                    # (F = hs/100 N, m = M/1000 kg)

ok <- (grid$M %% 100 == 0) &
      ((100 * grid$hs) %% grid$M == 0) &            # acceleration is a multiple of 0.1
      (grid$a10 %in% round(10 * a_allowed))         # ... and is one of the allowed values
grid <- grid[ok, ]

## pick the acceleration first (so every allowed value is equally likely),
## then pick a setup that produces it
a_values <- unique(grid$a10)
a_pick   <- a_values[sample(length(a_values), 1)]
rows     <- grid[grid$a10 == a_pick, ]
setup    <- rows[sample(nrow(rows), 1), ]

## quantities in kg and N
cart   <- setup$cart   / 1000
cargo  <- setup$cargo  / 1000
hanger <- setup$hanger / 1000
heft   <- setup$heft   / 1000
hs     <- setup$hs     / 1000          # hanger side mass, kg
force  <- setup$hs / 100               # forward force, N  (= hs in kg x 10 N/kg)
total  <- setup$M      / 1000          # total mass, kg
acc    <- setup$a10 / 10               # m/s^2  (= force / total)

## formatting helpers
kg  <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)                 # 0.05, 0.60, ...
num <- function(x) format(round(x, 3), trim = TRUE)   # 2, 1.5, ...
```

Question
========

A cart is pulled along a level track by a string that runs over a pulley to a hanger. Some mass (cargo) rides on the cart, and some mass (heft) sits on the hanger. Ignore friction and the mass of the string.

```{r diagram, echo = FALSE, fig.path = "", fig.cap = "", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 2.7}
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 10.5), ylim = c(0, 3.3), asp = 1,
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## track, cart, wheels
segments(0.2, 1.4, 7.0, 1.4, lwd = 3)
rect(1.0, 1.7, 3.6, 2.4, col = "grey95", lwd = 2)
symbols(c(1.5, 3.1), c(1.55, 1.55), circles = c(0.15, 0.15),
        inches = FALSE, add = TRUE, bg = "black")
text(2.3, 2.05, paste0("cart ", kg(cart), " kg"))

## cargo on the cart
rect(1.3, 2.4, 3.3, 3.1, col = "grey85", lwd = 2)
text(2.3, 2.75, paste0("cargo ", kg(cargo), " kg"))

## pulley and string
symbols(7.3, 1.7, circles = 0.3, inches = FALSE, add = TRUE, bg = "white", lwd = 2)
segments(3.6, 2.0, 7.3, 2.0, lwd = 1.5)
segments(7.6, 1.7, 7.6, 1.1, lwd = 1.5)

## hanger and heft
rect(7.2, 0.2, 8.0, 0.4, col = "black")
rect(7.3, 0.4, 7.9, 1.1, col = "grey85", lwd = 2)
text(8.2, 0.3, paste0("hanger ", kg(hanger), " kg"), adj = 0)
text(8.2, 0.8, paste0("heft ", kg(heft), " kg"), adj = 0)

## forward direction
# arrows(4.2, 1.0, 6.2, 1.0, length = 0.12, lwd = 2)
# text(5.2, 0.65, "forward")
```

* The **forward force** is the weight of the hanger plus the heft.
* Weight is found by multiplying mass by 10 N/kg.
* The **total mass** being pushed forward is made of all four masses: cart, cargo, hanger, and heft.

Answerlist
----------
* What is the forward force (in N)?
* What is the total mass (in kg)?
* What is the acceleration of the cart (in m/s$^2$)?

Solution
========

The forward force is the weight of the hanger plus the heft. Their total mass is
$`r kg(hanger)` + `r kg(heft)` = `r kg(hs)`$ kg, so the weight is
$`r kg(hs)` \times 10 = `r num(force)`$ N.

The total mass includes all four masses:
$`r kg(cart)` + `r kg(cargo)` + `r kg(hanger)` + `r kg(heft)` = `r kg(total)`$ kg.

The acceleration is the force divided by the total mass:
$`r num(force)` \div `r num(total)` = `r num(acc)`$ m/s$^2$.

* $(`r kg(hanger)` + `r kg(heft)`) \times 10 = `r num(force)`$ N
* $`r kg(cart)` + `r kg(cargo)` + `r kg(hanger)` + `r kg(heft)` = `r kg(total)`$ kg
* $`r num(force)` \div `r num(total)` = `r num(acc)`$ m/s$^2$
